“The sense of belonging to an online social community is driven by participation, community organisation and community satisfaction.
“Community integration is driven by community participation and organisation, and by community satisfaction.

“the sense of belongingness of members to an online community depends on the community’s satisfaction, participation and organization, and the interaction effects of these constructs with the degree of routinization”.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the drivers that influence the sense of belonging of a community.

the effects that the community satisfaction, participation, organisation and the routinisation of use have on the integration in the Tuentin community, and how these effects vary depending on the level of routinisation of the use.
the effects of community drivers on integration in a social networking site, and how these effects are moderated by routinisation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our research contributes to a better understanding of how to design and manage a social network community.

our research model can be used to evaluate and assess the impact of different strategic proposals related with participation, organisation and post-adoption satisfaction during the implementation of a social networking service.
community satisfaction and community participation are important drivers for the sense of integration in the online community.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

our research provides evidence that community satisfaction, participation, and community organisation are important factors in the development of social network sites and that routinisation is an important factor in determining the impact of these three factors on integration.
the community satisfaction is a crucial factor to consider in the development of a community.
the sense of belonging is determined by the community drivers, and that these drivers are affected by the level of routinisation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the community manager needs to focus on the post-implementation period to ensure the community members’ satisfaction and to avoid the negative impact of the community organisation.
the sense of belonging to an online community does not only depend on the initial acceptance, but it is also influenced by post-adoption phenomena, such as community satisfaction and routinisation.
the impact of community characteristics on the sense of community belongingness is not constant over time.
